description: Long before I knew the word "GPS" existed, I wanted to know exactly where my father was. He was out of station, on his way home, and my child-brain had decided that his location must be something you could look up. I knew one book that contained every unknown word: the dictionary. So I seriously asked my mother to search for his location in it. She laughed and called me Suppandi — the Tinkle character famous for perfectly literal, perfectly wrong logic. The nickname faded. The curiosity that earned it never did.

Then came years away from technology. I prepared for JEE Mains, took a drop year to try again, and didn't make it. I won't dress that up as a victory — it was a failure, and it was lonely. But somewhere in that quiet I learned a distinction I still use today: isolation is something that happens to you, solitude is something you build. I rebuilt myself in that solitude — slower, calmer, and certain that the curious kid with the dictionary was still in there, waiting for a terminal.

Today I study Computer Science with a specialization in AI & ML, finally giving that old curiosity a proper toolbox. I build small projects on purpose — e-vivlio, Yard, Cove, this portfolio — because shipping is how I think. Yard taught me WebSockets and Web Audio by making strangers hear the same song at the same second; Cove taught me WebRTC by turning a room code into a voice call with screen share, no login required. At night I fall down browser rabbit holes: WebGL, Web Audio, WebSockets, and whatever the spec drafts next. I'm planning higher studies in AI/ML, and I'm actively looking for hard problems and good collaborators. If that sounds like something you're building, my inbox is one scroll away.
